title: EquiCAD: A Geometric Equivariant Neural Network for 3D Shape Classiﬁcation
claim: A multi-branch architecture combines symmetry-aware encoders with graph reasoning, processing parts and their relations into one unified representation.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, dashed module boxes, color-coded feature bars
description: A left-to-right architecture diagram. At the left, a Data Processing box takes a gray CAD cylinder. It splits the cylinder into surface patches (S1), an adjacency matrix drawn as a green grid, and an intersection curve of S1 and S2. Blue arrows feed the surface and curve data into two stacked dashed boxes, Surface Encoder and Curve Encoder. Each box has a Main Road: EquiNN, showing spherical-harmonic blobs for l and m and a tensor-product network, plus a Branch: CNN drawn as orange conv blocks. Blue (surface) and pink (curve) feature bars flow into a central pink-outlined fusion graph. The adjacency matrix arrow joins there. The output goes to a Graph Encoder box showing node and edge updates, then to the classification output vector. A legend sits at top right.
caption: Overview of the proposed EquiCAD framework. Our approach extracts meaningful features of B-rep models through three synergistic steps: (1) an SO(3)/O(3)-equivariant encoder that preserves geometric symmetries, (2) an auxiliary CNN branch operating on invariantized equivariant features to capture local UV-space patterns, and (3) a graph neural network that aggregates topological relationships. Feature fusion combines invariant embeddings before message passing produces the ﬁnal graph-level embedding for classiﬁcation.
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) shape classification plays a central role in computer vision and computer-aided design (CAD), underpinning applications in intelligent manufacturing, automated inspection, and digital engineering. Despite recent progress with 3D CNNs and graph-based approaches, existing methods often overlook the geometric-topological regularities and symmetry principles intrinsic to CAD boundary representations (B-reps). To address this challenge, we introduce EquiCAD, a symmetry-aware learning framework that integrates equivariant representations with graph-based reasoning. By leveraging group-theoretic decomposition of curve and surface descriptors, EquiCAD preserves symmetry-consistent feature transformations while retaining rich geometric details. The model further exploits hierarchical message passing to capture interactions between local features and global structure. Experimental results across multiple datasets, including SolidLetters, Parts, the Machining Feature benchmark, and our newly constructed Features dataset, demonstrate substantial improvements over prior state-of-the-art approaches, particularly on industrially relevant shapes with fine-grained attributes. These findings highlight the value of symmetry-aware modeling for robust and generalizable 3D shape analysis.
